candidate_reports.remark: The Bird Springs chapter house reported flooding overtopped the N-71 bridge near N-2. Road and bridge are still flooded as of around 11 AM the following (Thursday) morning_ along with an estimated 38 houses/properties impacted in the Transwestern Rd area about 5 miles west of Bird Springs.
Mesonet station QHBA3 Humbug Creek.
ASOS station KFLG Flagstaff Airport.
Mesonet station AV601 Bellemont.
Mesonet station DVI020197 GREENS PEAK SITE 6B.
Mesonet station AZT25 Cerro Montosa.
Mesonet station AU373 Snowbowl.
Mesonet station ASBSB Arizona Snowbowl Pumphouse.
Mesonet station AZT12 Hwy 377 @ 14 Mile Hill MM 376.
ASOS station KINW Winslow Airport.
Mesonet station JE065 2.2 S Holbrook (JE-FULLER).
Mesonet station AZT24 Kendrick Park.
USGS river gauge on the Paria River at Lees Ferry (PLFA3) reported a 3.37 foot rise in 30 minutes from upstream heavy rainfall_ with a peak discharge of 2_285 cfs.
Stream gauge on Chinle Creek showed a 2.5 ft rise_ reaching flood stage. Flooding reported in Chinle and Canyon de Chelly.
Report from mPING: Half-inch (0.50 in.).
A former NWS employee reported dozens of 1-2 ft diameter ponderosa pine trees down in the forest. Some trees were snapped. Time is estimated based on radar signatures.

An EF1 rated tornado developed south of Walker and traveled north-northeast across Walker Road. The estimated maximum wind speed was 105 mph along its 8 mile path. Maximum width was estimated to be 300 yards.
Corrects previous tstm wnd gst report from 4 ESE Prescott Courthouse. Yavapai County Sheriff office reported 5 downed trees on Walker Road near mile marker 4 near Lynx Lake.
Report from Wednesday morning. Yavapai Sheriff Office reported trees down and caused closure of Walker Rd around mile post 4.
ASOS station KFLG Flagstaff Airport.
Public reported hail up to the size of ping pong balls. Dents observed in a truck.
Public reported hail up the size of half dollars.
Former NWS employee reported quarter sized hail in the Cheshire neighborhood.
Corrects previous hail report from 1 N Downtown Flagstaff. Public reported_ via Facebook_ hail up to the size of quarters.
Public reported hail up to the size of half dollars.
Public reported hail up to the size of half dollars. Hail accumulation on the ground.
Corrects previous hail report from 2 N Flagstaff Airport. Public reported_ via Facebook_ hail up to the size of ping pong balls.
A NWS employee reported hail up to the size of ping pong balls.
Corrects previous hail report from 2 WSW Downtown Flagstaff. Public reported via Facebook hail up to the size of golf balls.
Public reported_ via Facebook_ hail up to the size of quarters.

A USGS stream gauge on the Moenkopi Wash reported an 8 ft rise in 15 minutes at 10:30 AM. Water levels continued to rise all afternoon reaching a 13 ft rise by 4:53 pm with a flow of about 13_400 cfs. KAFF News also shared photos on Facebook of flooding in the Hopi village of Moenkopi.
Public reported_ via Facebook_ hail up to the size of ping pong balls.
Law enforcement reported downed trees on Walker Road between mile markers 3 and 4 near Lynx Lake.
Public reported via Facebook hail up to the size of golf balls.
Report from mPING: Quarter (1.00 in.).

*** 1 INJ *** Approximate start point of an EF-1 rated tornado that moved north through the Heber-Overgaard area. Peak winds estimated to be 110 mph along its 11 minute journey. The path was just over 9 miles with maximum width estimated to be around 350 yards. There was 1 non life-threatening injury reported.

*** 1 INJ *** 46 structures sustained damaged in Heber-Overgaard. There was 1 non life-threatening injury to a bicyclist. Time of report is estimated by radar. Further information will be provided after damage assessments are completed.
River gauge on Paria River indicated a rapid 5 foot rise_ eventually reaching 3800 cfs by 4 AM MST.
Photo of hail from social media.
Video showing water flowing over a bridge in the Pinon area. Road is impassable.
Navajo Nation DOT reports a washed out culver on BIA 591 in the Kayenta area. The road is impassable.
Numerous low water crossings along Oak Creek impassable in the Sedona area. Oak Creek stream gauge in Sedona crested at 2 PM at 5500 cfs.
Report from NWS Flagstaff Facebook page.
Navajo Nation DOT reports flooding on N6460 and N6461 in Dennehotso as water in Laguna Creek is overtopping the banks of the creek.
Navajo Nation DOT reports N8027 near Hardrock is closed due to an exposed culvert/washed out road.
Report from NWS Flagstaff X page.
Funnel cloud reported west of Sedona. Photo shared via NWS Flagstaff X Page.
Stream gauge on Fossil Creek indicated a 5 foot rise between noon and 1 PM MST.
Stream gauge on West Clear Creek indicated a rapid 5 foot rise.
Navajo Fire reports flooding of homes near N6460 and N6461 in Dennehotso. Evacuations and water rescues of 30 people taking place near Laguna Creek.
Report via NWS Flagstaff X page.
Navajo Nation DOT reports N21 in Kaibeto closed due to the road and culvert being washed out.
Navajo Nation DOT reports N9092 has been washed out and is extremely muddy.
Report via NWS Flagstaff X page.
Updated to reflect larger hail size based on photo with measurement. Hail sizes reported between 0.75-1.75". Report via NWS Flagstaff X page.
Gauge on Wet Beaver Creek indicated a rapid 5 foot rise_ reaching flood stage.
Navajo Nation DOT reports partial washout of N33 in the Cove Chapter area.
Navajo Nation DOT reports water flowing across N12 in Hunters Point.
Navajo Nation DOT reports multiple washouts along N4 between Pinon and H43.
Swift water rescue on flooded Wet Beaver Creek near Dragonshead Rd and Culpepper Ranch Rd.
Two photos of hail sent to NWS Flagstaff. One showed quarter size hail with a quarter for a comparison. Second showed larger hail estimated to be around 2 inches.
Navajo Nation DOT reports N4 and N8031 in Pinon is currently flooding and the road has been damaged on N8031.
Navajo Nation DOT reports that a culvert on N8033 in Forest Lake has been washed out and the roadway has collapsed.
Navajo Nation DOT reports N8066 in Black Mesa was partially washed out and is extremely muddy along the route.
ADOT reports US 89 northbound closed near Bitter Springs (MP 528) due to boulders from a rockfall caused by heavy rain.
Navajo Nation DOT reports the road and bridge on the west side on N35 in Sweetwater is currently washing out. The bridge has been compromised and the road is closed.
ADOT reports SR-87 northbound closed due to flooding at MP 398.
NWS employee reported significant flow in Wet Beaver Creek near Lacy Lane. Road is impassable.

ADOT reporting water on and near US-89 Southbound near BIA-20 (MP 498). Nearby spotter at Bodaway Gap Chapter House stated water is decreasing from yesterday. Reported several dirt roads were washed out with water from nearby wash affecting residential homes nearby.
